name: Major cyber incidents
summary: Refrigeration control attacks hit EU supermarkets for a second time; Binance theft largest on record
state: Attackers reset internet-exposed refrigeration controllers at supermarkets across Europe overnight into 2 Nov, a second wave after attacks in France about three weeks earlier; Danfoss said its products were involved and Carrefour Belgium counted 15 stores hit (The Hacker News). The FBI attributes the roughly $6.3bn Binance theft to North Korea. No national-scale outage of power, health or finance systems was reported as of 5 Nov.
for_you: Organisations running internet-connected building or refrigeration controls should follow NCSC or CISA guidance and patch exposed systems.
rubric_hit: Attacks disrupting large retailers in several countries = Watch; no national-scale outage

sources.title: The Hacker News — New wave of refrigeration cyberattacks hits supermarkets across Europe

why: Ransomware and state hacking now shut down hospitals, retailers, carmakers and airports for weeks.
drivers: Ransomware gangs, state actors, zero-days, supply-chain compromises.

rubric.alert: National-scale attack on critical infrastructure (power, health, finance), or a destructive state-attributed attack.
rubric.watch: Ransomware or attack disrupting a large company or critical service, or a mass-exploited zero-day.
rubric.normal: No major incidents disrupting critical services this week.
